introduction: Explore Jotunheim’s rival courts, follow its proof requests and choose how to spend scarce materials. Eleven independent stories and four service or rejection responses use exact items. New discovery and progress require active, ready accounting.
orientation: ENTER Yggdrasil from the Astral Plane to reach Jotunheim. The tree in Jotunheim provides the return journey. The foggy downward path is not another usable destination. Hostile giants, mountain flight and water travel remain dangerous.

Find Mimir behind the hidden boulder passage in the Vinsaar mountains. ASK mimir task explains his two proof requests. His well’s legends are lore; drinking from it or learning a skill does not complete either request. For Mimir’s first request, bring the intricate golden amulet worn by the high shaman of Kostchtchie. The raven gloves are the reward; finding those gloves elsewhere does not record this hand-in.

Mimir’s larger request needs five different items together: the frost mage’s jade bracelet, the Balor’s lightning sword and barbed whip, the shaman’s rose-quartz shield, and the sapphire and gold bracelet lying among the stone huts. Five similar-looking pieces or a single leader’s proof will not do.

The Balor’s lightning sword can go to Mimir’s five-item request or Quelranor’s fiend request. Once it is spent, you need another actual sword for the other request. Recovering the sword or surviving the Balor’s death blast does not complete either quest. Quelranor accepts the Balor’s jagged lightning sword for the holy gauntlets of the planetar and experience, then leaves. His proof is the same sword needed by Mimir’s five-item bundle. Gifts of the exact sword fit without personal combat history.

Mimir rejects the blood-splattered fur leggings and the nightshade bracelet. These replies are listed for clarity and earn no story achievement or daily credit. Do not give those items expecting a quest reward.

At the fluting metal gate, SAY kostchtchie, then OPEN gate and go SOUTH when the route is closed. The plain iron key carried by a frost mage at the gate opens the alchemist’s storeroom. You may also find the hidden stone stairway and the tear behind the elegant tent. An already open route does not require your own earlier gate action.

Fireweed grows on the trail just below Mount Siva’s basalt outpost. Bring the actual clump to the frost giant alchemist for an earring and experience. Fireweed does not survive ordinary rent/save handling; keep your current supply in view. The advertised Muspelheim passage is unfinished.

Brimir in Okalnir carries the heavy pewter tankard. Bring that exact tankard to the drow emissary in Utgard. The request accepts its identity; do not assume it checks how much ale remains or records a separate brewing action.

At Utgard’s western wall, inspect the broken sign. SAY silverwing, then OPEN illusion and go EAST when the route is closed. The northern portcullis has no working entrance. The sign’s badge warning does not add a badge requirement to this spoken route.

The blacksmith in Utgard’s marketplace offers two remorhaz-scale recipes. Ordinary and ancient scales are different materials, even though they look similar on the ground. Each recipe also costs 250 platinum and is currently unavailable while accounting is active. Both remain services. Ordinary remorhaz carry the ordinary scales; the rare ancient remorhaz carries the ancient scales. These are carried stock, rather than CARVE rewards. Removing an ingredient from a container is preparation, without proving a personal kill.

Brunnhilde, Sarimar, Grishnar, Rashnik, Olaf Forkbeard and Quelranor may wander through Jotunheim. Their presence depends on the current rare inhabitants; a listed request does not promise its giver is available. ASK the named contact when you find them.

Brunnhilde accepts Sarimar’s belt of human skulls for the antlered mask of Valhalla and experience. This is separate from her request concerning Silverwing. She remains after the belt hand-in, but leaves after accepting Silverwing’s cloak. Silverwing is Telshanar, the shackled movanic deva in Utgard’s royal hall. The cloak of deva’s feathers is the exact proof Brunnhilde accepts. Her response mourns his absence; it does not record freeing, escorting or healing him. Wearing the cloak does not satisfy the loose-item preparation check.

Sarimar accepts Brunnhilde’s flaming sword of the valkyrie for a bloody minotaur’s rib cage and experience, then leaves. His bounty and Brunnhilde’s bounty are independent opposing requests; a matching supplied proof fits without your own kill.

Grishnar asks for Rashnik’s sacred snow-troll totem. Rashnik asks for Grishnar’s feathered ice-troll standard. Each giver leaves after the accepted exchange; both award the claws of the destroyer. Owning the shared reward does not identify which request you completed. Olaf Forkbeard accepts the hideous red leather mask worn by the head overseer in the mining hills, then leaves after rewarding you. His words call you dwarf-friend, but the quest records this proof exchange without a separate slave rescue or lasting faction change.

Thrym’s rune-covered stone, Mimir’s epic training, the blacksmith’s additional forging, the wells and other shops described in scenery are separate services or lore. Epic training and forging have their own restrictions and accounting guards. The journal does not manufacture quest outcomes from them. Fearfrost on the Elemental Plane of Air owns the four-item request for Frostbite, Mistweave, a token of allegiance to Thrym and the Maelstrom fragment. Mundorno in Alatorin can produce the same white-dragon leggings found here. Those foreign exchanges belong to their own journals; possessing their materials or rewards here does not complete them.

All eleven story requests are potential dailies under current rules. Exact current stock, legitimate item supply and the return of departing givers govern availability. The requests are independent; the journal requires no earlier personal travel, kill or different story receipt.
